items.title: SMF: N7 create policy association response handling failure leaves orphaned associations at the PCF
items.body:
### Summary

The SMF creates an SM policy association at the PCF when a PDU session is established, and deletes it by calling `remove_sm_policy_association()`. That delete call exists in exactly one place: `handle_pdu_session_release_complete()`, which runs only when the UE sends a PDU Session Release Complete NAS message. The AMF-driven path, `handle_pdu_session_release_sm_context_request()`, contains no policy handling at all.

So when a session is torn down through the AMF, the SMF completes the release without ever telling the PCF to drop the association. The association stays at the PCF, and the SMF has moved on. Nothing in the deployment signals that anything was left behind, because the session itself ended normally.

### Details

`v2.2.1` (April 2026), SMF commit `53af440`.

**There is only one delete call site, and it sits behind a specific NAS message.**

`remove_sm_policy_association()` is called from exactly one place in the SMF, inside `handle_pdu_session_release_complete()`:

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L1686-L1692

That function has one caller, reached only under `case kPduSessionReleaseComplete`, which is step 3 of the UE-initiated release procedure:

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L2199-L2215

**The AMF-driven release path never reaches it.** The Release SM Context Request the AMF sends is handled here, and this function contains no policy handling, no delete, and no `n7::` call at all:

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L2740-L2800

### PoC

Full stack (`v2.2.1`), no source change, no injected condition. A real PCF, a real SMF, and one UE that establishes a PDU session and then disconnects. Associations at the PCF are counted as created minus deleted.

**The leak.** One UE session was established and torn down. The PCF created 12 associations for it and deleted none. The SMF sent 12 create requests over N7 and zero deletes; the PCF received no DELETE at all. The SMF handled the teardown normally, logging `Handle Release SM Context Request from AMF` and completing the release, so this is not a failed or aborted session. It ended cleanly and the associations stayed.

(12 rather than 1 because the SMF retransmits the create during establishment. The SMF's create count and the PCF's created count match per session, so every retransmission becomes another association.)

**The accumulation.** Repeating the same establish-and-disconnect cycle:

```
             PCF created | PCF deleted
start                  0 |  0
session 1             12 |  0
session 2             25 |  0
session 3             37 |  0
after teardown        37 |  0
```

The count only rises. `deleted` stays at 0 through every session and stays at 0 after the last teardown, so nothing reclaims them later either. Association IDs are unique per create, so a new session adds entries rather than replacing old ones. The only bound is the lifetime of the PCF process.

### Impact

A PCF policy association survives at the PCF every time a PDU session is released through the AMF, which is the ordinary teardown path. No unusual configuration, no proxy, no failure injection: a UE that establishes a session and disconnects leaves associations behind, and the PCF's table grows with the number of sessions the deployment has served.

The session itself succeeds and ends cleanly, so nothing surfaces the problem. The SMF does not log a failed delete, because it never attempts one.

Deletion is implemented, and appears to work as intended when a UE drives the release itself with a PDU Session Release Complete. The gap is that the AMF-driven release path does not share that cleanup.

items.title: A restarted SMF reuses SM context references, so an old reference from the AMF releases another UE's PDU session
items.body:
### Description

The SMF gives SM context references (`smContextRef`) from a counter that starts at 0 on every start (`smf_app::generate_smf_context_ref()`, `src/smf_app/smf_app.cpp`, develop b2374073; `uint_generator` in common-src). A restarted SMF therefore hands out references 1, 2, ... again.

The AMF does not learn that the SMF restarted, so it keeps the references from the previous run for PDU sessions that the SMF has lost. When the AMF later uses one of them, for example to release the SM context when the UE deregisters, the request reaches the new SM context that has the same reference. That context belongs to another UE. The SMF releases it, and the other UE loses its PDU session without being told.

TS 29.501 clause 4.4.1 says "A URI uniquely identifies a resource". The SM context URI is `{apiRoot}/nsmf-pdusession/<apiVersion>/sm-contexts/{smContextRef}` (TS 29.502 clause 6.1.3.3.2). A reference from the previous run should find no context (404 `CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND`, TS 29.502 clause 6.1.7.3), not the context of another UE.

### Expected behavior

After an SMF restart, a request with a reference from the previous run gets 404. The PDU sessions created after the restart are not affected.

### Observed behavior

The request releases the PDU session of another UE.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the core (AMF, SMF, UPF) and attach two UEs, A and B. Note the SM context reference that B got (AMF log `Stored SMF context_location`), for example `sm-contexts/1`.
2. Restart the SMF container (`docker restart oai-smf`). We also restarted the UPF, so that its old PFCP sessions do not reject the new ones (see oai-cn5g-upf#41).
3. Restart UE A so that it registers again and gets a new PDU session. A is the first new session, so it gets `sm-contexts/1`.
4. Stop UE B. B sends a Deregistration Request.

### Logs

OAI gNB and 4 nrUEs in RF simulator mode. AMF and SMF are v2.2.2 with local patches for stale UE contexts and stale PDU sessions. None of them changes how SM context references are given out or looked up. Before the SMF restart, UE 0832 (B) had `sm-contexts/1`. After the restart, UE 16069 (A) registered again:

```
[amf_sbi] [debug] Stored SMF context_location for PDU Session ID 10, SUPI imsi-262990100016069: http://192.168.71.133:80/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1
```

Then UE 0832 was stopped. The AMF released its old reference, and the SMF found the context of UE 16069:

```
[amf_sbi] [info] Send HTTP message to http://192.168.71.133:80/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/1/release
[amf_sbi] [info] Get response with HTTP code (204)
[smf_app] [debug] Retrieve SMF context with SUPI imsi-262990100016069
[smf_app] [info] PDU Session Release SM Context accepted by UPFs
[smf_app] [info] Resources associated with this PDU Session have been released
```

Before UE 0832 was stopped, UE 16069 received 3 of 3 pings to the DN. After it, UE 16069 received 0 of 3. UE 16069 still had its IP address, so it did not know that its session was gone.

The same happens without a UE restart in step 3: any UE that gets a reused reference can lose its session when the AMF uses an old reference. Step 3 only makes the order of the references known.

### Related points

These are not part of this issue:

- The AMF could detect the restart and drop the old contexts. TS 23.527 clause 6.3 and TS 29.502 clause 6.1.6.2.3 (`recoveryTime` and `smfServiceInstanceId` in `SmContextCreatedData`) give it the information. TS 23.527 clause 6.1 leaves the clean-up to the implementation.
- When the UPF rejects the N4 Session Establishment, the SMF sends the PDU Session Establishment Reject but does not send `Nsmf_PDUSession_SMContextStatusNotify` (Release) to the AMF (TS 23.502 clause 4.3.2.2.1 step 18). Its context stays, marked inactive (`smf_app::handle_itti_msg(itti_sbi_n1n2_message_transfer_response_status&)`), and the AMF keeps the reference. In our test, this was how the AMF came to hold an old reference for a UE that had no session.

A fix follows in a pull request.

items.title: SMF crashes when a UE retries a PDU session that was rejected before UPF selection (null session graph)
items.body:
### Description

`session_handler::deallocate_resources()` dereferences `m_session_graph` with no check (`src/smf_app/session_handler.cpp`, develop 3f6e9dda). The graph is null for a PDU session that was rejected before UPF selection. Since #17, such a session can reach this function: the SMF crashes (null pointer dereference) when the UE asks again for the same PDU Session ID.

The path on `develop`:

1. `smf_context::handle_pdu_session_create_sm_context_request()` adds the `smf_pdu_session` with a `session_handler` but no graph (`add_pdu_session()`).
2. The request is rejected before the graph is set: no free UE IP address (`get_free_paa()` fails), or no UPF (`session_create_sm_context_procedure::run()` returns `ERROR` before `set_session_graph()`). The session object stays in the context, and its SM context reference, created in `smf_app` Step 8 before the context handles the request, stays too (see also #12).
3. The UE sends a new PDU Session Establishment Request with the same PDU Session ID (`INITIAL_REQUEST`). `smf_app` Step 5 (added by #17) finds the stale reference and calls `stale_session->deallocate_ressources()`, which calls `m_session_handler->deallocate_resources()`.
4. `m_session_graph->get_access_edges()` on a null `shared_ptr`.

`get_all_qfis()` in the same class already returns early when the graph is not set ("this may be called when session graph is not set due to error procedure").

A second defect sits behind the crash on the no-UPF path. The UE IP address is assigned to the session (`sp->set(paa)`) before the procedure runs. When the procedure fails, Step 10 returns the address to the pool but leaves `sp->ipv4` set. Once the crash is fixed, the release in Step 5 returns the same address to the pool again (`release_paa(dnn, ipv4_address)`), possibly while another UE holds it, and the pool can then hand it out twice.

### Expected behavior

The stale rejected session is replaced. Its UE IP address, if it had one, was returned to the pool once, at the reject. No PDR, QER, FAR or URR IDs are released because it has none.

### Observed behavior

`deallocate_resources()` dereferences the null graph. A unit test that calls it on a `session_handler` without a graph crashes with SIGSEGV.

### Steps to reproduce

We found this in review and reproduced it with a unit test, not on a live core. From the code, these steps reach it:

1. Start the SMF with no UPF associated (or with a UE IP pool that is full).
2. Send a PDU Session Establishment Request for a UE. The SMF rejects it.
3. Send it again with the same PDU Session ID.

Unit test (in `src/smf_app/test/test_session_handler.cpp`):

```cpp
session_handler handler(pdu_session_type_e::PDU_SESSION_TYPE_E_IPV4);
handler.deallocate_resources();  // SIGSEGV
```

### Logs

`docker build --target checks` on `develop` (3f6e9dda) with only the test added (arm64 host):

```
[ RUN      ] SessionHandlerTest.DeallocateResources_WithoutSessionGraph_DoesNothing
28/32 Test #28: SessionHandlerTest.DeallocateResources_WithoutSessionGraph_DoesNothing ...***Exception: SegFault  0.09 sec
97% tests passed, 1 tests failed out of 32
```

A fix for both, with this test, follows in a pull request.

items.title: SMF: IP address allocation failure in PDU session establishment may accumulate SMF PDU session contexts
items.body:
### Summary

The SMF registers an `smf_pdu_session` into the SM context before it has an IP address for it.
When address allocation then fails, `smf_context::handle_pdu_session_create_sm_context_request()` sends a PDU Session Establishment Reject and returns without calling the release API, `smf_context::remove_pdu_session()`. The session object stays live in `smf_context::pdu_sessions` for a PDU session the UE was already told had failed.

The only cleanup that touches it is collision handling for a *new* INITIAL_REQUEST on the same identity, which is not a rollback of the failed request. The PoC confirms one surviving object per PDU session identity and zero releases on the error path.

### Details

Source analysis on `v2.2.1` (April 2026), SMF commit `53af440`.

**1. The session is registered before the address is allocated**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L857-L871

`smf_context::add_pdu_session()` inserts it into `pdu_sessions`, keyed by PDU session identity. From here `find_pdu_session()` and every consumer of the SM context sees it.

**2. The failure point**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L996-L1010

Four more early returns in the same function follow the registration and have the same shape: `:978` (IPv4v6, pool exhausted), `:1027` and `:1042` (PDU session type not supported), `:1059` (unknown type).

**3. The release API is never reached.**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L3447-L3452

`smf_context::remove_pdu_session()` has one call site outside the context class:

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_app.cpp#L1073-L1080

That is collision handling — it fires when a new INITIAL_REQUEST arrives for an identity that already has a session and an SCID mapping. It is not cleanup for a request that failed, and a survivor that never reached SCID creation is not covered by it. Nothing unwinds the registration on the reject path itself.

### PoC

The `default` DNN pool was set to a `/30` so address allocation runs out. One UE then attempts several PDU sessions. No source change.

```
contexts registered ("PDU Session Id (N) has been added successfully") : 33
rejects             ("Could not get PAA ... for DNN default")          : 33
contexts removed    (remove_pdu_session debug line)                    : 31
net still in the map                                                   :  2
```

Counts of SMF log lines over one run, from a freshly started SMF.

- **The error path never releases.** Every registration is followed by a reject, and no removal ever follows one. All 33 registrations leaked at the point of failure.
- **The removals come from the next request, not from the failure.** Each removal in the log is preceded by a fresh INITIAL_REQUEST and the `PDU Session already existed` warning from `smf_app.cpp:1077` — the collision cleanup. The UE retransmitted on the same identity, and that retransmission is what cleared the previous object.
- **What is left over stays.** Once the requests stop, the last object on each identity has nothing to clear it and remains in `pdu_sessions` until the `smf_context` is destroyed. The run used identities 1 and 2 and ended with 2 objects still there.

A single attempt, with no removal between registration and reject:

```
01:06:18.674 [smf_app][info]    Add PDU Session with Id 2
01:06:18.675 [smf_app][debug]   PDU Session Id (2) has been added successfully
01:06:18.675 [smf_app][warning] Could not get PAA PDU_SESSION_TYPE_E_IPV4 for DNN default
01:06:18.675 [smf_n1 ][info]    Create N1 SM Container, PDU Session Establishment Reject
```

### Impact


Address pool exhaustion needs no unusual configuration to reach: a busy DNN, a pool sized for fewer subscribers than attach, or addresses held by sessions that were never released all end at the same get_free_paa() failure. While that lasts, every PDU session attempt leaves an object behind.

The object is usually short-lived, because the UE's own retransmission clears it. The collision cleanup at smf_app.cpp:1073 runs before the handler, so the next INITIAL_REQUEST on that identity removes the previous object and the handler builds a fresh one. That is what the PoC shows: 33 registrations against 33 rejects, with 31 removals all attributable to a following request.

What is not guaranteed is that anything ever clears it. Nothing in the failure path does, and the collision cleanup only runs if another INITIAL_REQUEST arrives on the same identity. When the UE gives up, or moves to a different identity, the object stays in pdu_sessions until the smf_context is destroyed. The run ended with 2 such objects, one per identity used.

Memory growth is bounded by the PDU session identity space per UE, and everything is freed with the smf_context.

items.title: After a UE deregisters and registers again, the PDU session reuses the released object and its UE IP address is never returned to the pool
items.body:
### Description

After #17, a UE that deregisters and registers again with the same PDU Session ID gets a session whose UE IP address is never returned to the pool. Each deregistration and registration cycle loses one address.

The cycle on `develop` (3f6e9dda):

1. UE-initiated deregistration. The AMF sends Release SM Context. The SMF releases the session: `deallocate_ressources()` returns the UE IP, sets `resources_deallocated`, and `clear()` empties the session. d1a6b824 (#17) then removes the session's SM context reference. The cleared `smf_pdu_session` object itself stays in the SM context.
2. The UE registers again and sends a PDU Session Establishment Request with the same PDU Session ID (`INITIAL_REQUEST`). `smf_app` Step 5 runs only when `scids_2_smf_context()` finds a reference, which is gone, so the stale object is not replaced. The context finds the existing object ("PDU session is already existed!") and reuses it for the new session, with `resources_deallocated` still set.
3. The next release of that session returns at once with "Resources associated with this PDU Session were already released". The new UE IP address is not returned to the pool.

### Expected behavior

After a deregistration and a new registration, the UE gets the same IP address again (it was returned to the pool), and the old session object is replaced.

### Observed behavior

The UE gets a new IP address on each cycle, and the SMF logs "already released" on each release.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register a UE with a PDU session (we used OAI rfsim with nrUE).
2. Deregister it (UE-initiated, e.g. stop the nrUE cleanly) and start it again. Repeat.

### Logs

SMF v2.2.2 with the two commits of #17 cherry-picked (the same code as `develop` for this path). One nrUE, three cycles:

```
UE tunnel address after each restart: 12.1.1.4 -> 12.1.1.6 -> 12.1.1.7
[00:03:31.972] [smf_app] [info] Resources associated with this PDU Session have been released
[00:03:47.415] [smf_app] [warning] PDU session is already existed!
	PAA IPv4:		12.1.1.4
[00:03:50.483] [smf_app] [debug] Resources associated with this PDU Session were already released
[00:04:00.854] [smf_app] [warning] PDU session is already existed!
	PAA IPv4:		12.1.1.6
[00:04:03.838] [smf_app] [debug] Resources associated with this PDU Session were already released
[00:04:16.064] [smf_app] [warning] PDU session is already existed!
	PAA IPv4:		12.1.1.7
```

With the fix that follows in a pull request, the same three cycles kept 12.1.1.4 each time, with "replaced stale session" on each cycle and ping to the UE working.
